Happy National Girls and Women in Sports Day from Clemson Womens' Soccer 🐾

Today, February 4th, is National Girls and Women in Sport Day, and to honor #ngwsd, the RHBSSI is highlighting seven female student-athletes from all different Clemson sports! 

What does it mean to be a woman in sports?

“Being a woman in sports means being strong, resilient, and unstoppable,” Sade Gray, @clemsontrackxc, Marketing major 

“Being a woman in sports is all about representation and feeling confident in myself,” Bianca Martinez, @clemsontrackxc, @clemsonvb, Sociology major

“Being a woman in sports means having a big community of strong and inspirational women to look up to,” Madison Roush, @clemsontrackxc, Biomedical Engineering major

“Being a woman in sports means showing up with strength, discipline, and confidence in spaces that haven’t always made room for us,” Tatum Short @clemsonwsoccer, Psychology major 

“It means embracing the pressure that comes with higher expectations and learning how to carry myself with purpose both in competition and in everyday life,” Trinity Webb, @clemsongymnastics, Communications major

“It means overcoming challenges, proving my abilities, and staying confident in spaces where women are sometimes underestimated,” Shaunque Williams, @clemsontrackxc, Psychology major, RHBSSI Intern

“Being a woman in sports means pursuing passion and excellence while often overcoming inequality and stereotypes,” Oneka Wilson, @clemsontrackxc, Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management major

Click the link in our bio to learn more about their stories as women in sport!

So thankful for the amazing women that make up Clemson University Rowing. 🐅💜

We’re excited to feature our team doctor, Dr. Tenley (Palisin) Murphy, for our next alumni shoutout! ✨ We are so grateful to have a team doctor who understands our sport and shares our love for Clemson! 

Dr. Murphy’s journey is nothing short of remarkable:
🐅 Member of the inaugural Clemson Women’s Rowing team (Class of 2001)
🐅 University of South Carolina School of Medicine graduate (2005)
🐅 Completed a Sports Medicine fellowship following residency
🐅 Currently serves as Assistant Athletic Director of Sports Medicine at Clemson
🐅 One of the first women in sports medicine to serve as a Power 5 team physician 🔥
🐅 Has supported countless Clemson successes, including the Women’s Soccer College Cup, National Championships in Men’s Soccer, multiple ACC titles in Softball and Track

Dr. Murphy shared, “It’s been an incredible journey through sports medicine to provide care to our student-athletes, support them in their endeavors, and celebrate their successes.”

She is deeply grateful for the support of her husband, Dr. Brett Murphy, and their amazing daughter, Addison (13).

Thank you, Dr. Murphy, for all that you do for our team — and for continuing to inspire Clemson student-athletes on and off the water. 🧡💜🐅
